title: 1 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 20.

questions.question: From where did David flee before speaking to Jonathan?
options: Naioth in Ramah
Bethlehem
Gibeah
Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Naioth in Ramah
questions.explanation: David fled from Naioth in Ramah, as stated in 1 Samuel 20:1.

questions.question: What was David's concern when he approached Jonathan?
options: Why Jonathan was angry
What iniquity or sin he had done to Saul
How to become king
Where to hide next
questions.correctAnswer: What iniquity or sin he had done to Saul
questions.explanation: David asked Jonathan what he had done, what his iniquity was, and what his sin was before Saul, since Saul sought his life (1 Samuel 20:1).

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan believed that his father would do great things without telling him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonathan said that his father would not do anything great or small without telling him first (1 Samuel 20:2).

questions.question: What did David swear by when he spoke to Jonathan about the danger he was in?
options: The king's life
The LORD and Jonathan's soul
The covenant
His own life
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD and Jonathan's soul
questions.explanation: David swore by the LORD and Jonathan's soul that there was but a step between him and death (1 Samuel 20:3).

questions.question: What promise did Jonathan make to David in response to his request?
options: He will hide him
Whatever David's soul desires, he will do it
He will fight Saul
He will send him away
questions.correctAnswer: Whatever David's soul desires, he will do it
questions.explanation: Jonathan told David that he would do whatever his soul desired (1 Samuel 20:4).

questions.question: What event was happening the next day that David said he should not miss?
options: The new moon
The yearly sacrifice
The king's feast
A battle
questions.correctAnswer: The new moon
questions.explanation: David mentioned that the new moon was the next day and he should sit with the king at meat (1 Samuel 20:5).

questions.question: For how many days did David plan to hide himself in the field?
options: One day
Two days
Three days
Four days
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: David planned to hide himself in the field until the third day at evening (1 Samuel 20:5).

questions.question: True or False: David instructed Jonathan to say he was going to Bethlehem for a yearly sacrifice if Saul missed him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: David told Jonathan that if his father missed him, Jonathan should say David went to Bethlehem for the yearly sacrifice (1 Samuel 20:6).

questions.question: What would it mean if Saul responded with anger when Jonathan spoke about David's absence?
options: David was sick
Good things were planned for David
Evil was determined by Saul against David
Jonathan should leave the city
questions.correctAnswer: Evil was determined by Saul against David
questions.explanation: Jonathan said if Saul was very wroth, then evil was determined by him (1 Samuel 20:7).

questions.question: What did David say Jonathan should do if there was any iniquity in him?
options: Tell Saul immediately
Slay David himself
Ignore it
Send David away
questions.correctAnswer: Slay David himself
questions.explanation: David said Jonathan should slay him himself if there was any iniquity in him (1 Samuel 20:8).

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan said he would not tell David if Saul planned evil against him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonathan said if he knew that Saul planned evil against David, he would tell him (1 Samuel 20:9).

questions.question: What did Jonathan and David do together after their conversation about Saul's intentions?
options: Went to the city
Went out into the field
Prayed together
Went to Saul's court
questions.correctAnswer: Went out into the field
questions.explanation: Jonathan said to David, "Come, and let us go out into the field," and they went both out into the field (1 Samuel 20:11).

questions.question: What did Jonathan say he would do to find out Saul's intentions about David?
options: Ask the king directly
Sound his father about David on the new moon or third day
Send a messenger to David
Hide David in the city
questions.correctAnswer: Sound his father about David on the new moon or third day
questions.explanation: Jonathan said he would sound his father about David on the new moon or the third day (1 Samuel 20:12).

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan promised to send David away in peace if Saul planned evil against him.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan promised that if his father planned evil, he would show it to David and send him away in peace (1 Samuel 20:13).

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 20, which instruction comes first?
options: David should hide in the field for three days
Jonathan should sound his father about David on the new moon
Jonathan and David should go out into the field together
David should tell Saul he went to Bethlehem for a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: David should hide in the field for three days
questions.explanation: David first requested to hide in the field for three days (1 Samuel 20:5) before Jonathan planned to sound his father or they went out into the field (1 Samuel 20:11-12).

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What covenant did Jonathan make with the house of David as described in 1 Samuel 20?
options: A covenant that the LORD will require vengeance on David's enemies
A covenant of peace between Saul and David
A covenant to make David king immediately
A covenant to reveal Saul's plans to David
questions.correctAnswer: A covenant that the LORD will require vengeance on David's enemies
questions.explanation: Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, 'Let the LORD even require it at the hand of David's enemies' (1 Samuel 20:16). This shows his loyalty and protection towards David's house.

questions.question: How did Jonathan express his love for David according to 1 Samuel 20?
options: He caused David to swear again because he loved him as his own soul
He gave David a royal position
He promised to protect David from Saul alone
He sent David away to another city
questions.correctAnswer: He caused David to swear again because he loved him as his own soul
questions.explanation: Jonathan caused David to swear again because he loved him; the text says he loved David as he loved his own soul (1 Samuel 20:17). This highlights the depth of their friendship and loyalty.

questions.question: What significance did Jonathan place on the new moon festival regarding David's absence?
options: David would be missed because his seat would be empty
David would be honored with a feast in his absence
David was expected to lead the festival
David was to be publicly accused
questions.correctAnswer: David would be missed because his seat would be empty
questions.explanation: Jonathan told David that on the new moon, he would be missed because his seat would be empty, indicating David’s usual attendance and the significance of his absence (1 Samuel 20:18).

questions.question: What was the purpose of Jonathan shooting three arrows in the field?
options: To signal David whether it was safe to return or not
To practice archery skills with a young lad
To celebrate the new moon festival
To warn Saul of David's hiding place
questions.correctAnswer: To signal David whether it was safe to return or not
questions.explanation: Jonathan planned to shoot three arrows in the field and send a lad to find them. Depending on where he told the lad the arrows were, David would know if it was safe to come or if he needed to flee (1 Samuel 20:20-22).

questions.question: What did Jonathan say would happen if his father intended to do evil to David?
options: He would inform David and send him away in peace
He would defend David openly to Saul
He would join his father in persecuting David
He would remain silent to protect his father
questions.correctAnswer: He would inform David and send him away in peace
questions.explanation: Jonathan said if it pleased his father to do evil to David, he would show it to David and send him away so he might go in peace (1 Samuel 20:13).

questions.question: What attitude of Saul toward David's absence is described in 1 Samuel 20:26?
options: Saul said nothing but thought David was not clean
Saul rejoiced at David's absence
Saul suspected Jonathan had hidden David
Saul immediately ordered a search for David
questions.correctAnswer: Saul said nothing but thought David was not clean
questions.explanation: Saul did not speak that day but thought, 'Something hath befallen him, he is not clean; surely he is not clean,' showing his suspicion without verbal accusation (1 Samuel 20:26).

questions.question: How did Jonathan explain David’s absence to Saul?
options: David asked leave to go to Bethlehem for a family sacrifice
David was ill and could not attend the meal
David was on a secret mission for the king
David was avoiding Saul intentionally
questions.correctAnswer: David asked leave to go to Bethlehem for a family sacrifice
questions.explanation: Jonathan told Saul that David earnestly asked leave to go to Bethlehem because of a yearly family sacrifice there, which explained David’s absence (1 Samuel 20:28-29).

questions.question: What was Saul’s reaction upon learning David was absent for the meal from Jonathan?
options: He was angry and accused Jonathan of choosing David to his own confusion
He accepted the explanation and wished David well
He sent Jonathan to find David immediately
He ignored the absence and changed the topic
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry and accused Jonathan of choosing David to his own confusion
questions.explanation: Saul’s anger was kindled, and he accused Jonathan of choosing David to his own confusion and the confusion of his mother’s nakedness as a result (1 Samuel 20:30).

questions.question: What did Saul command regarding David’s fate once he learned of his absence?
options: To fetch David to him so he could kill him
To forgive David and welcome him back
To exile David from the kingdom
To imprison David in the palace
questions.correctAnswer: To fetch David to him so he could kill him
questions.explanation: Saul commanded to send and fetch David because he said he would surely die as long as David lived upon the ground (1 Samuel 20:31).

questions.question: How did Jonathan respond when Saul threatened to kill David?
options: He questioned why David should be slain and what he had done
He agreed with Saul and distanced himself from David
He remained silent out of fear
He pleaded with David to leave the kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why David should be slain and what he had done
questions.explanation: Jonathan asked Saul, 'Wherefore shall he be slain? what hath he done?' showing his concern and defense of David (1 Samuel 20:32).

questions.question: What was Jonathan’s emotional response after Saul’s anger and threat toward David?
options: He arose in fierce anger and did not eat meat the second day of the month
He celebrated with the king despite Saul’s anger
He immediately informed David to flee
He went to mourn privately without eating for a week
questions.correctAnswer: He arose in fierce anger and did not eat meat the second day of the month
questions.explanation: Jonathan was grieved for David and in fierce anger, arose from the table and did not eat meat the second day of the month (1 Samuel 20:34).

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 20:23 teach about the relationship between Jonathan and David?
options: The LORD is between them forever, signifying a lasting bond
They agreed to keep their plan secret from Saul
They decided to fight Saul together
They promised to never see each other again
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is between them forever, signifying a lasting bond
questions.explanation: Jonathan said, 'the LORD be between thee and me for ever,' indicating a covenantal and enduring relationship (1 Samuel 20:23).

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan sent a lad to find the arrows Jonathan had shot as a secret signal to David.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan sent a lad to find the arrows he shot as a way to secretly communicate to David whether it was safe to come or not (1 Samuel 20:21, 1 Samuel 20:36).

questions.question: True or False: Saul spoke loudly and angrily at the meal when David’s seat was found empty the first night of the new moon festival.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Saul did not speak anything on that day but thought to himself that something had befallen David and that he was not clean (1 Samuel 20:26).

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Samuel 20, Jonathan’s kindness to David was to continue even after Jonathan’s death and the LORD’s judgment on David’s enemies.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan asked David not to cut off kindness from his house forever, even after the LORD had cut off David’s enemies (1 Samuel 20:15).

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 20.

questions.question: What reason did David give Jonathan for not attending the king's table at the new moon feast?
options: He wanted to hide in the field until the third day at even
He was sick and unable to come
He was summoned to fight in battle
He was attending a family sacrifice in Bethlehem
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to hide in the field until the third day at even
questions.explanation: David told Jonathan he should not fail to sit with the king at meat on the new moon but requested to hide in the field until the third day at even (1 Samuel 20:5).

questions.question: How did Saul react when Jonathan explained David's absence from the king's table?
options: He was angry and accused Jonathan of choosing David over him
He accepted the explanation and wished David well
He ordered Jonathan to bring David to him immediately
He ignored Jonathan and ate in silence
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry and accused Jonathan of choosing David over him
questions.explanation: Saul's anger was kindled against Jonathan and he accused him of choosing the son of Jesse to his own confusion and his mother's nakedness (1 Samuel 20:30).

questions.question: What was Jonathan’s response when Saul ordered him to fetch David to kill him?
options: He asked Saul why David should be slain and what he had done
He immediately obeyed and went to find David
He refused and fled the palace
He agreed to discuss David’s fate later
questions.correctAnswer: He asked Saul why David should be slain and what he had done
questions.explanation: Jonathan asked his father why David should be slain and what wrong he had done (1 Samuel 20:32).

questions.question: What did Saul do to express his anger towards Jonathan during their exchange about David?
options: He cast a javelin at Jonathan to smite him
He shouted loudly and cursed Jonathan
He sent guards to arrest Jonathan
He ordered Jonathan to leave the palace
questions.correctAnswer: He cast a javelin at Jonathan to smite him
questions.explanation: Saul cast a javelin at Jonathan to smite him, showing his fierce anger and determination to kill David (1 Samuel 20:33).

questions.question: What did Jonathan do after Saul’s violent outburst against him?
options: He arose in fierce anger and ate no meat the second day of the month
He immediately sought reconciliation with Saul
He fled to David in the field
He confronted Saul publicly
questions.correctAnswer: He arose in fierce anger and ate no meat the second day of the month
questions.explanation: Jonathan was grieved for David because his father had shamed him, so he arose in fierce anger and did not eat the second day of the month (1 Samuel 20:34).

questions.question: What sign did Jonathan use to secretly communicate to David whether it was safe to return to the city?
options: He would shoot three arrows and send a lad to find them
He would send a message with a servant
He would light a signal fire on the hill
He would wave a white cloth at David's hiding place
questions.correctAnswer: He would shoot three arrows and send a lad to find them
questions.explanation: Jonathan told David he would shoot three arrows in the field and send a lad to find them; the location of the arrows would signal whether David could safely return (1 Samuel 20:20-22).

questions.question: What literary device is used in the secret arrow signal between Jonathan and David in 1 Samuel 20?
options: Foreshadowing
Chiasm
Parallelism
Typology
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: The secret arrow signal foreshadows the impending danger and the protective covenant between Jonathan and David, highlighting the tension and impending conflict (1 Samuel 20:20-22).

questions.question: What covenant did Jonathan make with David concerning their families?
options: Not to cut off kindness from each other's households forever
To serve in the same army
To share all their possessions
To marry into each other's families
questions.correctAnswer: Not to cut off kindness from each other's households forever
questions.explanation: Jonathan made a covenant with David that kindness would not be cut off from David's house forever, even after Jonathan died (1 Samuel 20:15-16).

questions.question: How did David express his feelings when he and Jonathan parted after the arrow signal?
options: They kissed and wept until David exceeded
They shook hands and promised to meet again
David bowed silently and left
Jonathan gave David a token of remembrance
questions.correctAnswer: They kissed and wept until David exceeded
questions.explanation: After the lad left, David arose, bowed to the ground three times, and they kissed and wept until David exceeded (1 Samuel 20:41).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'iniquity' in 1 Samuel 20:1 mean in the original language?
options: Moral wrongdoing or sin
Physical illness
Ignorance
Punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Moral wrongdoing or sin
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'iniquity' (עָוֹן, avon) generally refers to moral wrongdoing or sin, indicating David's concern about what sinful act caused Saul to seek his life (1 Samuel 20:1).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of covenant loyalty seen between Jonathan and David?
options: Ruth 1:16-17 - Ruth's loyalty to Naomi
Genesis 1:1 - Creation of the world
Exodus 20:1-17 - The Ten Commandments
Psalm 23 - The Lord is my shepherd
questions.correctAnswer: Ruth 1:16-17 - Ruth's loyalty to Naomi
questions.explanation: Ruth 1:16-17 reflects covenant loyalty similar to Jonathan's commitment to David, emphasizing steadfast love and faithfulness even in difficult circumstances (1 Samuel 20:14-17).

questions.question: What does the covenant between Jonathan and David foreshadow in the broader biblical narrative?
options: The enduring Davidic covenant and God's faithfulness to David's lineage
The destruction of Saul's family
The exile of Israel to Babylon
The coming of the Messiah from Saul's line
questions.correctAnswer: The enduring Davidic covenant and God's faithfulness to David's lineage
questions.explanation: The covenant foreshadows God's enduring promise to David and his descendants, highlighting the divine plan for David's house despite Saul's opposition (1 Samuel 20:15-16; 2 Samuel 7:12-16).

questions.question: What cultural practice does David mention as the reason for his planned absence to Jonathan?
options: A yearly family sacrifice in Bethlehem
A military conscription
A royal feast in Ramah
A pilgrimage to the temple
questions.correctAnswer: A yearly family sacrifice in Bethlehem
questions.explanation: David told Jonathan that the family had a yearly sacrifice in Bethlehem, which was the reason he asked to be excused (1 Samuel 20:29).

questions.question: True or False: Jonathan was unaware of Saul’s intention to kill David until Saul threatened his own son with a javelin.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonathan realized Saul intended to kill David when Saul cast a javelin at him, confirming his father’s determination (1 Samuel 20:33).

questions.question: True or False: The lad who retrieved the arrows knew the meaning of the signal between Jonathan and David.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The lad was unaware of the significance of the arrows; only Jonathan and David knew the meaning of the signal (1 Samuel 20:39).

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Jonathan's assurance to David in 1 Samuel 20:2 reveal about Jonathan's trust in God's providence and his father Saul's character?
options: Jonathan believes Saul will secretly harm David without warning
Jonathan trusts that Saul will inform him of any plans against David
Jonathan doubts Saul's intentions but hopes for the best
Jonathan thinks David is guilty of a serious sin
questions.correctAnswer: Jonathan trusts that Saul will inform him of any plans against David
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 20:2 shows Jonathan's confidence that his father will not do anything great or small without telling him, indicating trust in God's providence and Saul's transparency toward Jonathan.

questions.question: Which doctrine concerning human sinfulness and divine judgment can be derived from David's statement in 1 Samuel 20:3 about the proximity of death?
options: The doctrine of original sin
The doctrine of sanctification
The doctrine of human depravity and the reality of imminent judgment
The doctrine of predestination
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of human depravity and the reality of imminent judgment
questions.explanation: David acknowledges the closeness of death due to iniquity in 1 Samuel 20:3, illustrating human depravity and the serious consequences of sin under divine judgment.

questions.question: How does Jonathan's covenant with David in 1 Samuel 20:16 reflect the biblical teaching on covenantal loyalty and divine justice?
options: It shows human promises are unreliable
It reflects an unconditional love without accountability
It demonstrates loyalty bound by God's justice, holding enemies accountable
It is a political agreement rather than a spiritual one
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates loyalty bound by God's justice, holding enemies accountable
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 20:16, Jonathan makes a covenant invoking the LORD to require it from David's enemies, showing loyalty grounded in divine justice and accountability.

questions.question: What theological insight about friendship and love does 1 Samuel 20:17 provide through Jonathan's declaration of love for David?
options: Friendship is based on mutual gain
True love in friendship mirrors the love one has for their own soul
Friendship is superficial and temporary
Love should be conditional on circumstances
questions.correctAnswer: True love in friendship mirrors the love one has for their own soul
questions.explanation: Jonathan's statement in 1 Samuel 20:17 reveals a profound love for David, comparable to the love he has for his own soul, highlighting biblical ideals of deep, covenantal friendship.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 20:23, Jonathan says, 'the LORD be between thee and me for ever.' What attribute of God is demonstrated in this mutual invocation?
options: God's omnipotence
God's covenant faithfulness
God's wrath
God's transcendence
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Jonathan invokes the LORD as the witness between him and David forever in 1 Samuel 20:23, underscoring God's attribute of covenant faithfulness and the binding nature of divine promises.

questions.question: How does Saul's reaction to David's absence in 1 Samuel 20:26 and 1 Samuel 20:30 illustrate the human sin of jealousy and its consequences?
options: Saul shows righteous indignation toward David
Saul's jealousy leads to anger and unjust accusations against Jonathan and David
Saul is indifferent to David's whereabouts
Saul seeks peaceful reconciliation
questions.correctAnswer: Saul's jealousy leads to anger and unjust accusations against Jonathan and David
questions.explanation: The verses 1 Samuel 20:26 and 20:30 reveal Saul's jealousy manifesting as anger and harsh words, demonstrating the destructive nature of envy in human relationships.

questions.question: What does Jonathan's protective strategy involving arrows in 1 Samuel 20:20-22 teach about divine guidance and human agency in the face of danger?
options: It shows reliance solely on human planning without faith
It illustrates the interplay of human action under divine providence
It is a magical ritual
It indicates distrust between friends
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the interplay of human action under divine providence
questions.explanation: Jonathan's plan with arrows in 1 Samuel 20:20-22 demonstrates human planning combined with trust in God's guidance, showing how divine providence works through human agency.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth about covenant loyalty and divine protection is conveyed by synthesizing 1 Samuel 20:14-15 and 1 Samuel 20:41-42?
options: Covenant loyalty is temporary and self-serving
God's protection is independent of human relationships
Covenant loyalty reflects God's enduring kindness and divine peace between friends
Human covenants are unreliable and bring sorrow
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant loyalty reflects God's enduring kindness and divine peace between friends
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 emphasize ongoing kindness and covenant loyalty, while verses 41-42 show their emotional and spiritual depth, together teaching that covenant loyalty mirrors God's enduring kindness and peace.

questions.question: How does David's hiding in the field and Jonathan's sending of a lad in 1 Samuel 20:19 and 35-40 demonstrate the biblical principle of discernment in spiritual conflict?
options: It shows avoidance of all conflict
It illustrates strategic discernment and use of subtle signs to communicate danger
It promotes open confrontation without caution
It relies on luck rather than wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates strategic discernment and use of subtle signs to communicate danger
questions.explanation: David's hiding (20:19) and Jonathan's use of coded signals via a lad (20:35-40) embody the biblical principle of discerning and wisely navigating spiritual or physical danger.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's justice and human responsibility can be drawn from Jonathan's willingness in 1 Samuel 20:8 to kill David if he found him guilty of iniquity?
options: Doctrine of divine sovereignty without human accountability
Doctrine of human responsibility under God's moral law
Doctrine of universal salvation
Doctrine of indulgence
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of human responsibility under God's moral law
questions.explanation: Jonathan's statement in 1 Samuel 20:8 shows that even close relationships are subject to justice and moral accountability, reflecting human responsibility before God’s law.

questions.question: How does the narrative arc involving Saul's intent to kill David in 1 Samuel 20:31-33 contribute to the broader biblical theme of the suffering servant and God’s chosen king?
options: It shows the futility of God's plans
It prefigures Christ's persecution and David as a messianic type
It undermines the concept of divine election
It focuses only on political intrigue
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures Christ's persecution and David as a messianic type
questions.explanation: Saul's intent to kill David (20:31-33) echoes the suffering servant motif, foreshadowing Christ’s persecution and David’s role as a messianic figure in redemption history.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the intense friendship between Jonathan and David in 1 Samuel 20 is merely political alliance rather than genuine loyalty. What does 1 Samuel 20:17 and 20:41-42 actually teach about the nature of their relationship?
options: Their relationship was purely political with no emotional depth
Their covenant and emotional expressions show genuine, sacrificial love and loyalty
They were rivals competing for the throne
Their friendship was superficial and short-lived
questions.correctAnswer: Their covenant and emotional expressions show genuine, sacrificial love and loyalty
questions.explanation: Jonathan's love as his own soul (20:17) and their weeping and kissing (20:41-42) demonstrate a genuine, sacrificial covenant relationship beyond mere political convenience.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by Jonathan's prayer invoking the LORD's presence between him and David forever in 1 Samuel 20:23?
options: God's mercy
God's omnipresence
God's covenant faithfulness
God's wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Jonathan's invocation in 1 Samuel 20:23 highlights God's covenant faithfulness as the eternal witness and guarantor of their agreement.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about divine protection and human responsibility is conveyed by synthesizing 1 Samuel 20:1-4 and 1 Samuel 20:41-42?
options: God protects without human cooperation
Human responsibility is irrelevant to divine protection
Divine protection operates through covenant loyalty and faithful human action
Human actions negate God's protection
questions.correctAnswer: Divine protection operates through covenant loyalty and faithful human action
questions.explanation: David's appeal to Jonathan (20:1-4) and their covenant renewal (20:41-42) together reveal that God's protection is manifested through human covenant loyalty and faithful relationships.

questions.question: How does the episode of Jonathan's anger and refusal to eat in 1 Samuel 20:34 deepen our understanding of the human cost of sin and broken fellowship?
options: It shows Jonathan's selfishness
It reveals the grief and anguish caused by familial and covenantal betrayal
It teaches that anger is always sinful
It suggests Jonathan was indifferent to David's plight
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the grief and anguish caused by familial and covenantal betrayal
questions.explanation: Jonathan's reaction in 1 Samuel 20:34 illustrates the deep emotional pain and broken fellowship resulting from Saul's hostile actions against David, reflecting the human cost of sin in relationships.
